operations.message: push_rear(20) → element arrives at the REAR (right) end — amber pointer
push_rear(30) → REAR pointer advances right to index 4
push_rear(40) → REAR pointer advances right to index 5
push_front(10) → element arrives at the FRONT (left) end — blue pointer moves left to index 2
Both ends are active: FRONT (blue) at [2], REAR (amber) at [5]
Unlike a regular queue, we can push AND pop from either end
pop_rear() → 40 leaves from the REAR — amber pointer retracts left to index 4
pop_front() → 10 leaves from the FRONT — blue pointer advances right to index 3
push_front(5) → new element enters at FRONT again — blue pointer moves to index 1
push_rear(99) → REAR grows back to index 5. Deque spans [1]→[2]→[3]→[4]→[5]
